title: The AI System as Closed-System Test Bed: Operations from Lagrange Observatory! on the Inference-Time Forward Pass (EA-SEI-MM-AI-01 v2.0, Framework 15 Paper 02)
creator: Nobel Glas
description:
EA-SEI-MM-AI-01 v2.0 proposes the fixed inference-time forward pass of an open-weight language model as a bounded test environment for the Semantic Deviation Principle. The paper carefully distinguishes observational closure—frozen weights, vocabulary, logits, and reproducible inputs—from any claim that a model is an ontologically closed world.

It defines signed local deviation as realized token surprisal minus the conditional distribution’s entropy, with net and absolute aggregates in bits per token. It separately defines continuation-field deformation by sampling model outputs with and without an intervention. Three pre-registered tests address corpus separation, in-context or fine-tuning deformation, and the companion deviation-optimized model experiment. The paper’s strongest conjecture is that formulaic AI prose will exhibit negative net deviation, while more distinctive writing will exhibit positive net deviation.

The document reports no results. Its equations are operational proposals whose interpretation depends on checkpoint, tokenizer, genre, sampling regime, corpus labels, and reference-model calibration. Although an earlier section narrows the argument to one predictable failure mode, a later claim again says cross-entropy “structurally minimizes meaning”; that categorical formulation exceeds the protocol’s own more careful account and should be repaired.

wiki_article:
**The AI System as Closed-System Test Bed** is a methods paper by Nobel Glas that translates the Semantic Deviation Principle into quantities measurable from language-model probabilities.

The first quantity compares each realized token’s surprisal with the model’s expected surprisal at that position. Positive values indicate a token less expected than the model’s baseline; negative values indicate convergence toward highly probable continuation. A second, more expensive quantity compares sampled future continuations with and without a contextual intervention.

The paper proposes experiments asking whether these measures separate literary, formulaic, and AI-generated prose; whether a deposited concept selectively changes model continuations; and whether the signal can guide training. The Crimson Hexagonal Archive corpus is treated separately to reduce self-validation.

The work is a pre-registration rather than a finding. “Meaning,” “slop,” and “deviation” remain operational terms inside the experiment, not quantities already shown to correspond to literary or human significance.
